objects.name: Chipkin Example B-AEC
objects.note: the device itself; the instance is configurable with --deviceID. The stack rows are device-wide facts only the stack knows - the protocol version and revision it implements, the services and object types it was configured with (17 base objects plus the dynamically creatable Analog Value), the live object list and address-binding table. The accepted rows are the stack's configured defaults for APDU limits, segmentation, system status and database revision; an application that answered them from its own constants could contradict the stack, so this example does not

objects.name: Bronze
objects.note: REAL, degrees Celsius; starts at 21.5. F-COVM: Present_Value AND Status_Flags are both marked subscribable (SetPropertySubscribable), so a SubscribeCOVPropertyMultiple naming both fires one multi-property notification when the up/down keys nudge this value

objects.name: Chartreuse
objects.note: F-OUTPUTS (NEW vs B-EM; canonical pattern from B-SA-CPP). REAL setpoint, 16-slot Priority_Array + Relinquish_Default (20.0); commandable. Present_Value itself is resolved by the stack from the Priority_Array - this application's Get callback answers the individual array-index reads (and Relinquish_Default) rather than Present_Value directly, exactly as B-SA's canonical pattern documents

objects.name: Fuchsia
objects.note: F-OUTPUTS (NEW vs B-EM). Active/inactive, commandable; Relinquish_Default inactive (0). Out-of-range writes (anything but 0/1) are rejected with value-out-of-range

objects.name: Indigo
objects.note: F-OUTPUTS (NEW vs B-EM). State 1..3, commandable; Relinquish_Default state 1. Out-of-range writes (state 0 or >3) are rejected with value-out-of-range. Verified by wire test: WriteProperty of state 9 rejected with value-out-of-range

objects.name: Vermilion
objects.note: BACnet/IP; Network_Type and Protocol_Level are set from BACnetStack_AddNetworkPortObject()'s arguments (IPv4, BACnet Application) at start-up, not a GetProperty callback like the object's other app-served rows; Changes_Pending is likewise computed and answered natively by the stack's Network Port object. Reliability has no fault condition this example detects, so it is accepted at the generic default (normal)

objects.name: Maroon
objects.note: F-ELEVATOR (canonical, from B-EM). Machine_Room_ID, Group_ID and Group_Members are NOT stack DEFAULTS - they are genuinely stored and served by BACnetStack_AddElevatorGroupObject (Group_Members is also maintained by BACnetStack_AddLiftOrEscalatorObject as Lift 1/Mauve is added to this group). They are marked accepted only because property-profile-reference.md's generic per-type table does not know about this object-specific host-configuration API and so cannot credit them as stack-served. isGroupOfLifts=true and supportLandingCallStatus=true: Group_Mode and LandingCalls are therefore also enabled (see the Lift's note for how the four F-ELEVATOR list/sequence callbacks are exercised) but property-profile-reference.md's generic Elevator Group table does not mark either 'required', so neither generates a checked row here - Group_Mode is served by GetPropertyEnumerated (normal) and LandingCalls by GetListElevatorGroupLandingCallStatus (no calls outstanding) regardless. NEW vs B-EM: Landing_Call_Control is now writable - BACnetStack_RegisterCallbackSetElevatorGroupLandingCallControl is registered (unlike B-EM, which deliberately left it unregistered), so a WriteProperty commanding a landing call is recorded and read back through GetListElevatorGroupLandingCallStatus. Code-reviewed against the stack's doc comment and confirmed to build/register correctly; NOT independently wire-verified with a real client in this session (BACnetLandingCallStatus's write-side SEQUENCE-CHOICE encoding is not cleanly expressible through the available test-client library) - flagged in the PR rather than assumed

objects.name: Mauve
objects.note: F-ELEVATOR (canonical). property-profile-reference.md's generated Lift table is INCOMPLETE relative to CASBACnetStackDLL.h's own doc comment for BACnetStack_AddLiftOrEscalatorObject (a documentation gap in the stack repo, not a stack API gap): the markdown table omits Car_Position, Car_Moving_Direction, Car_Door_Status, Passenger_Alarm, Out_Of_Service and Fault_Signals entirely, even though the DLL header lists all six as REQUIRED Lift properties. This example serves every one of them regardless, because they are genuinely required by clause 12.59 - Car_Position and Car_Moving_Direction via GetPropertyUnsignedInteger/GetPropertyEnumerated, Car_Door_Status (one door, index 1) via GetPropertyEnumerated with useArrayIndex, Passenger_Alarm and Out_Of_Service via GetPropertyBool, Fault_Signals (empty - no active faults) via the GetListOfEnumerations callback. Status_Flags, Elevator_Group, Group_ID and Installation_ID ARE in the generic table (stack-computed/stack-stored) and are accepted for the same reason as Maroon's. Passenger_Alarm is the AE-N-I-B alarm source: an intrinsic ChangeOfState(bool) algorithm routed to Notification Class 1 (Crimson); it is not writable through any API in this stack (a real installation drives it from hardware), so this example simulates it on a 30-second timer rather than a key or a write - see the file header comment in main.cpp. Optional properties Assigned_Landing_Calls, Registered_Car_Call and Landing_Door_Status are enabled and each exercises one of the four F-ELEVATOR list/sequence callbacks with one demonstration entry

objects.name: Mint
objects.note: F-ELEVATOR. Not a member of Maroon (a group of Lifts, isGroupOfLifts=true) - added with the spec's 'no reference' sentinel (4194303) for Elevator_Group, as clause 12.60.6 allows. Required Operation_Direction (no stack default), Passenger_Alarm and Out_Of_Service are served by the app; the optional Power_Mode and Escalator_Mode are enabled and served too, for a fuller demonstration. Status_Flags/Elevator_Group/Group_ID/Installation_ID are stack-stored, same reasoning as Mauve's

objects.name: Turquoise
objects.note: not one of the profile's named objects - added explicitly by this application, BEFORE Elevator Group 1 (Maroon), as the object Maroon's Machine_Room_ID references. BACnetStack_AddElevatorGroupObject's own doc comment reads as though the stack creates this object automatically if missing; verified against the running stack, it does not - AddElevatorGroupObject fails outright ('Create the Positive Integer Value object before adding the Elevator Group object') unless the application adds it first. Colour 'Turquoise' per docs/colour-table.md's global positive_integer_value mapping; Present_Value (required, no stack default) is served as an arbitrary plausible room id. Units defaults to no-units (accepted) since a machine-room identifier has none; Out_Of_Service is optional and left at the generic default

objects.name: Crimson
objects.note: AE-N-I-B / AE-ACK-B / AE-INFO-B. Priority, Ack_Required and Recipient_List are NOT stack DEFAULTS - they are genuinely populated by BACnetStack_AddNotificationClassObject (Priority, Ack_Required) and BACnetStack_AddRecipientToNotificationClass (Recipient_List) at start-up; marked accepted only because property-profile-reference.md's generic per-type table does not know about this object-specific host-configuration API. Unlike B-AAC (AE-CRL-B), Recipient_List is NOT made writable here - AE-CRL-B is not a required BIBB for this profile

objects.name: Beige
objects.note: AE-EL-I-B (F-EVENTLOG, NEW vs B-EC; this series' canonical pattern is B-ALSC-CPP). Enable/Buffer_Size/Record_Count/Total_Record_Count/Log_Buffer/Status_Flags/Object_Identifier/Object_Type/Property_List are NOT stack defaults in the generic sense - they are genuinely held and served by the stack's own Event Log engine (BACnetStack_AddEventLogObject), answered from stack storage BEFORE this file's Get*/Set* callbacks are ever consulted; marked accepted only because property-profile-reference.md's generic table does not know about this object-specific engine. VERIFIED over the wire with a live bacpypes3 client against THIS repository's own build: Object_Name (undefined, the stack's generic non-Device default - no callback serves it), Record_Count and Total_Record_Count (both 0) all read correctly. VERIFIED DEFECT, independently reproduced in this repository (chipkin/cas-bacnet-stack#2045, first found by B-ACC-CPP): adding this object alone causes a continuous, non-fatal 'Failed to set the date'/'Failed to set the time' internal log flood starting from the very first BACnetStack_Tick() - 200 occurrences of each line observed in a 5-second smoke test window. NOTE: B-ALSC-CPP's own task (same object, same BACnetStack_AddEventLogObject call, same stack pin) did NOT observe this flood and its TODO.md/objects.json make no mention of it - the two repositories' object combinations differ (this one also adds Schedule/Calendar/File/Backup-Restore/DM-OCD-B), so the trigger is not 'AddEventLogObject alone' as B-ACC's bisection concluded; it reproduces in at least one combination the same as B-ACC's (Event Log + Schedule/Calendar + File/Backup-Restore) and did not reproduce in B-ALSC's narrower one (Event Log + Schedule/Calendar, no File/Backup-Restore). Flagged in TODO.md with this comparison rather than re-asserting B-ACC's isolation claim unverified. The device otherwise keeps answering Who-Is/ReadProperty correctly throughout the flood (wire-verified)

objects.name: Saffron
objects.note: SCHED-I-B (F-SCHED-I, NEW vs B-EC; canonical pattern from B-AAC-CPP, copied via B-ALSC-CPP's more recent template). Present_Value, Effective_Period, Schedule_Default, List_Of_Object_Property_References, Priority_For_Writing and Status_Flags are NOT stack defaults - they are genuinely held and served by the stack's Schedule engine (BACnetStack_AddScheduleObject plus the BACnetStack_SetSchedule*/AddSchedule* configuration calls in main.cpp); it writes Analog Output 1 (Chartreuse) Present_Value at priority 8. One weekly transition (Monday 08:00) and one calendar-date exception (2026-12-25, inline calendar-entry form) are seeded at start-up. VERIFIED over the wire with a live bacpypes3 client: Object_Name (undefined) and Priority_For_Writing (8) both read back correctly

objects.name: Cream
objects.note: Exists for SCHED-I-B completeness alongside Saffron's exception, but its Date_List cannot be populated through the customer API (cas-bacnet-stack issue #963 - no read path for a Calendar object's Date_List; the only generic constructed-property callback is test-tool-only, same gap B-AAC/B-ALSC/B-ACC all document). Present_Value therefore always answers false rather than evaluating a Date_List that is never populated. VERIFIED over the wire: Present_Value read back as false (0)

objects.name: Ivory
objects.note: DM-BR-B (F-BACKUP, NEW vs B-EC; canonical pattern from B-ACC-CPP) backup/restore payload carrier - stream access, in-memory 4KB buffer via BACnetStack_RegisterCallbackReadFile/WriteFile. File_Type/File_Size/Modification_Date/Archive/Read_Only all have NO stack default per property-profile-reference.md and are all served here. VERIFIED over the wire: File_Size read back as 0 (empty file) - this repository's own build did NOT reproduce B-ACC-CPP's documented File_Size read-access-denied finding (TODO.md #5 / issue #2046); see TODO.md for the comparison. AtomicReadFile/AtomicWriteFile round-trip and the restore half of the backup/restore cycle were NOT exercised over the wire this session (carrying forward B-ACC's documented, unresolved gap there rather than re-testing it) - see TODO.md

objects.name: (created at runtime via DM-OCD-B; not present at start-up)
objects.note: DM-OCD-B (F-OCD, NEW vs B-EC and the headline addition of this repository - canonical for the whole series). Analog Value is the ONLY creatable object type (BACnetStack_SetObjectTypeCreatable); no Analog Value instance exists until a client creates one with CreateObject. This row documents instance 2 - the object created and verified in this session's live wire test, then deleted - not a base object present at start-up (it does not appear in the base Object_List). Present_Value is served entirely by this file's g_createdAnalogValues table (no stack default for a non-commandable Analog Value's Present_Value) and made writable at the object-TYPE level (BACnetStack_SetPropertyByObjectTypeWritable, since there is no per-instance object to configure before one is created). Object_Name/Units/Out_Of_Service/Event_State/Status_Flags are accepted at their generic stack defaults (Object_Name reads 'undefined', Units 'no-units') - this example does not attempt to let a client name or configure a newly-created object beyond Present_Value. VERIFIED over the wire with a live bacpypes3 client against this repository's own build: CreateObject(analog-value, 2) accepted (CreateObjectACK); the object then appears in Object_List; ReadProperty of Present_Value (0.0) and Object_Name (undefined) both succeed; WriteProperty of Present_Value to 42.5 accepted and reads back correctly; DeleteObject(analog-value, 2) accepted (SimpleACK); a subsequent ReadProperty of the deleted instance correctly answers Error(object: unknown-object); CreateObject(binary-input, 5) - a non-creatable type - is correctly rejected with a CreateObjectError, never reaching this file's CreateObject callback in a way that allocates anything
